segments.title: 第87章 你笨
segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Years Chapter 87: You're Dumb

Starting from Tuesday, Li Luo discovered something strange.

His deskmate, Yan Zhusheng, had been acting a little odd lately.

On one hand, he always felt that Yan Zhusheng had been lacking energy recently.

Every day, right from the start of morning self-study, she would look drowsy and fatigued, often dozing off.

Often, as soon as the bell rang for the end of class, she would slump onto her desk and fall asleep with a thud. Even when she was awake, she was always in a daze.

And at times like these, Li Luo always felt that the way Yan Zhusheng looked at him was a bit peculiar.

But when he asked her what was wrong, Yan Zhusheng would fall silent for a moment, shake her head, and go back to sleep.

This situation didn't improve until Friday morning.

Li Luo let out a breath, quite satisfied with the effectiveness of his routine. He had habitually stored the incorrect problems he had categorized and organized from yesterday into a dedicated room in his memory palace.

With his two weeks of hard work and the effects of the memory palace, the framework for his knowledge system of all high school subjects was gradually taking shape.

Just as Ying Chanxi had believed before the high school entrance exams, having a complete knowledge system framework was essential to go further on the path of learning.

Just as Li Luo exited his memory palace, he saw Yan Zhusheng walk into the classroom through the back door with her schoolbag and arrive at her seat. He immediately raised his eyebrows.

"What's up?" Li Luo asked, "You don't seem so sleepy today?"

"Mmm," Yan Zhusheng, looking much more energetic than the past few days, nodded. "I had a good sleep yesterday."

"Then why didn't you sleep well the last few days?" Li Luo asked curiously, "What on earth were you doing late at night? Did you have insomnia?"

"You've already asked the same question for several days."

"That's because you never answered me."

"But I think it's better not to say it directly," Yan Zhusheng looked at Li Luo with a sincere expression and then said, "Besides, even if I don't tell you, you'll definitely figure out the answer."

Li Luo: "...How am I supposed to know the answer if you don't tell me? Am I a mind reader?"

"You'll definitely know, anyway," Yan Zhusheng said with certainty. "If you don't know, it just means you're dumb."

Hearing this, Li Luo's face darkened instantly. "Since when did you switch to being a fortune teller?"

The matter concerning Yan Zhusheng was thus left unresolved.

Although Yan Zhusheng said he would definitely find out, Li Luo racked his brains but still couldn't figure out why Yan Zhusheng hadn't been sleeping well late at night for the past few days.

However, after that, Yan Zhusheng never appeared sleepy during the day again, so Li Luo stopped paying attention to it.

Since Yan Zhusheng didn't want to say, Li Luo didn't ask anymore.

She was a girl, after all. It was quite normal for her to have a little secret of her own from him.

And so, his first year of high school life entered a rare period of calm.

Li Luo would wake up every morning, wash up, make some breakfast in the kitchen, and call Xu Youyu and Ying Chanxi to get up.

The dishwashing was left to the two of them.

Then, the three of them would go to school together.

During morning self-study, he would organize his knowledge framework in his memory palace and chat with Yan Zhusheng in a draft notebook.

He would attend classes seriously in the morning, participate in the jogging exercises during the long break at ten o'clock, and on the way back to the classroom, he would ask Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu how they wanted to handle lunch.

If none of them had other plans, Li Luo would call Yan Zhusheng along to eat on the second floor of the cafeteria.

If they each had their own plans, Li Luo would either eat alone with Yan Zhusheng, or be dragged off by Zhu Yufei and the others to play basketball.

Alternatively, he would find Zhao Rongjun, make up some excuse to scrounge a meal, or generously act as a sugar daddy and treat him to a good meal.

After lunch, Li Luo had to go to a classroom on the top floor of the second-year building to attend a student council meeting with his classmate and the Youth League branch secretary, Shi Yanran.

Originally, during the second week of school, the one presiding over the meeting was still the third-year student council president, Xue Yongbin.

But by the end of the third week, the person presiding over the meetings gradually became Xu Youyu.

When they chatted casually at home in private, Li Luo had already taken to addressing her as "Madam President." She would roll her eyes at him with a "heh," but she never denied it.

It was pretty much a done deal that Xu Youyu would take over as president after the National Day holiday.

After the routine noon meeting ended, Li Luo would return to the classroom for a nap, then continue to attend classes seriously in the afternoon.

After class, if the Math Club's workload wasn't heavy, Ying Chanxi would come find Li Luo and drag him over to the Literature Club for a visit.

If Ying Chanxi went to the Math Club for tutoring, then Li Luo would go play basketball with Zhu Yufei and the others, or follow Yan Zhusheng to the Rock and Roll Club to hang out.

Although he hadn't formally joined the Rock and Roll Club, he had become a semi-unofficial member. When they were short-staffed during practice, Li Luo even went up and had a blast.

After dinner in the evening, he would return to the classroom for evening self-study, finish his homework in two periods, and then head home with Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu.

If they were hungry, he'd make a late-night snack to fill the bellies of the two little foodies at home. If not, they would go straight back to their rooms to shower, and then he would write his novel.

As the end of September approached, "I'm Really Not a Star" had reached about 400,000 words.

On September 28th, the average subscription count for "I'm Really Not a Star" officially broke the 3,000 mark, earning an electronic "Boutique" badge on the book's details page.

At the same time, Li Luo, under his author pseudonym "Chongsheng," was pulled into an author group chat by his editor, Qian Zhou.

The Urban Boutique Group?

Li Luo had written a "Boutique" level book in the entertainment genre in his past life, but that was after 2020.

Although an average of 3,000 subscriptions was still a very impressive achievement back then, it certainly couldn't compare to the present day in 2014.

To be able to write a "Boutique" novel in 2014, every single one of them was a future big shot.

Li Luo scrolled through the list of group members and couldn't help but be amazed.

There were quite a few familiar faces.

Don't look down on the status of web novelists; if you threw a stone into this group, you'd hit someone who could earn over ten thousand a month.

If you were lucky with your throw, you might hit a millionaire, or even a multimillionaire.

And they were different from traditional entrepreneurs.

A company owner might have a net worth of tens of millions, but that was the total value of all their assets combined. If you asked them to produce a few million, or even a few hundred thousand in cash flow immediately without affecting the company's operations, it might be a bit difficult.

But for a writer, royalties were cash flow; whatever they earned went straight into their pockets.

The status of web novelists wasn't yet prominent at this time. Qianjiang Province's Web Novelists Association had only just been established this year. In another few years, or a dozen years, this group of people would completely take off.

Qian Zhou: Do you know about the Writers' Association?

Chongsheng: A little. What's up?

Qian Zhou: Over in Qianjiang Province, led by the provincial Writers' Association, the country's first Web Novelists Association was just established this year.

Qian Zhou: The Web Novelists Association has been actively recruiting web novelists from within Qianjiang Province recently.

Qian Zhou: Someone from there contacted us at Qidian, wanting us to recommend some Qianjiang web novelists with good results.

Qian Zhou: I remember you're studying in Yuhang City, right? The Web Novelists Association headquarters is right there.

Qian Zhou: If you don't mind, I'll go ahead and report your name up.

Chongsheng: Is it okay even if I'm a minor?

Qian Zhou: Of course! It's for setting an example. A high school student writing part-time, produces a "Boutique" novel with his first book, earns over ten thousand a month. If it's handled well, you could get a lot of benefits.

Chongsheng: Then thank you, Editor.

Qian Zhou: You'd better keep it up, then. I have high hopes for you! I'll submit your name in a bit.

Chongsheng: Okay.

After chatting with his editor, Li Luo was still a bit stunned, not expecting to be able to join the Web Novelists Association so soon.

And what's more, it was in 2014, right when the Web Novelists Association was first established.

(End of this chapter)
